guide.summary: Internal tool for your own Zendesk account (self-serve, wait none); Public app for many Zendesk customers (app review, wait 1-3 weeks for new submissions; reports of longer).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Internal tool for your own Zendesk account (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app for many Zendesk customers (app review, wait 1-3 weeks for new submissions; reports of longer).

composio.note: Composio supplies a managed OAuth app for Zendesk, fine for prototypes. For launch to many customers, use your own Marketplace-approved app and global client.

need_own_app.answer: For prototypes, no: Composio's managed app works. For a launch serving multiple Zendesk customers, yes: Zendesk requires such apps to be Marketplace-reviewed and use a global OAuth client, and it says third-party apps may not use a customer's own OAuth client.
reasons: Zendesk requires apps for multiple customers to go through Marketplace review
The consent screen shows 'Composio wants to access your account' with the managed app
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own app gets a dedicated quota
Custom scopes may need your own app, since Composio's default scopes may not cover them

prerequisites.title: Zendesk admin access
prerequisites.detail: Creating a new OAuth client needs a Zendesk account with admin access.

prerequisites.title: Registered Marketplace organization
prerequisites.detail: Register your organization on the Marketplace developer portal and sign in before submitting an app. A Marketplace profile is optional but is reviewed with your first submission.

prerequisites.title: Development account with d3v- subdomain
prerequisites.detail: The global client request form only accepts subdomains with the d3v- prefix. A sponsored developer account can be requested.

prerequisites.title: Stripe setup for paid apps
prerequisites.detail: To charge for the app, connect your Stripe account to Zendesk's and enter your Stripe Integration id in your organization details.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your own client ID and secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard. For prototypes, the managed app can be used.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection succeeds.

steps.title: Create local OAuth client in Zendesk
steps.detail: An admin creates the OAuth client and registers the redirect URI. For a public app, the identifier must start with zdg-, use the exact production value, and every field must be filled.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret are in hand.

steps.title: Pick the minimum scopes
steps.detail: List the API endpoints the app calls and whether each needs read or write. Prepare the scope list for the request form.

steps.title: Save client secret and identifier
steps.detail: Note the secret and identifier before requesting the global client, because admin page access is lost after conversion.

steps.title: Request global OAuth client
steps.detail: In the Marketplace portal, choose Global OAuth, then Request new OAuth. Provide the d3v- subdomain and scopes.
steps.done_when: You receive an email and ticket reference.

steps.title: Prepare submission package
steps.detail: Prepare the app ZIP, branding-compliant assets, privacy policy URL and an optional GitHub link. Integration apps also need marketing assets and translation files.
steps.done_when: ZIP passes the automatic checks with no errors.

steps.title: Submit app and accept terms
steps.detail: Go to Submit a new app, answer compliance questions accurately, and agree to the terms.
steps.done_when: Submission is accepted by the portal.

steps.title: Wait for Zendesk review
steps.detail: Stated turnaround is 1-3 weeks for new apps. Recent reports show longer waits.
steps.done_when: Approval notice arrives and listing is published.

traps.title: Global client cannot be self-created or edited
traps.detail: Developers cannot create global OAuth clients; Zendesk grants them. Once approved, only Zendesk's Marketplace Operations Team can edit the client.

traps.title: Customer's own credentials are banned
traps.detail: Third-party apps, listed or not, may not use a customer's API token or their own OAuth client.

traps.title: Requested scopes become a hard limit
traps.detail: A scope outside the allowed set fails with a 400 invalid_scope error. Changing scopes after approval means contacting Zendesk Support.

traps.title: Global client request may be hidden or hard to find
traps.detail: A Zendesk employee said the option is hidden if the subdomain already has a global client. A 2021 report said a docs link led to a blank page.

traps.title: Switching to OAuth affects live customers
traps.detail: A hard cutover forces all customers to re-authorize at once; a soft cutover lets them keep the old method until they re-authorize. You must then submit an update to your listing.

traps.title: Global client covers only Support and Chat
traps.detail: The guidance applies to Zendesk Support and Chat (Agent Workspace enabled) accounts. Zendesk Sell needs a Multi-User Application, and Sunshine Conversations bots need a separate token.

traps.title: Token expiry is enforced
traps.detail: Access tokens are short-lived and need the refresh token. Once a token expiry is set, Zendesk enforces it.

traps.title: Naming and press rules
traps.detail: The client identifier must represent your product; generic names are not acceptable. In press material, say 'working with' rather than 'partnership' unless approved.

blockers.what_it_means: Zendesk staff said a surge of submissions pushed response times past normal SLAs.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit early and use the ticket reference or Zendesk Support to follow up. Consider a preview app for key customers.

blockers.what_it_means: The app requested a scope outside the global client's allowed scopes.
blockers.what_to_do: Request only allowed scopes, or ask Zendesk Support to update them.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare requested scopes with the approved list.

blockers.what_it_means: The redirect URI in the request must exactly match the one configured on the OAuth client.
blockers.what_to_do: Copy the exact redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the Zendesk client.

open_questions: Is an app that is not listed but connects to many customers allowed? Docs say distribution to multiple customers needs Marketplace review; confirm with Zendesk Marketplace support.
What exactly does the review check beyond security and listing content? Not documented; ask Zendesk Marketplace support or check the submission checklist.
Current real review times after the OAuth-guideline backlog are unknown; check the Zendesk developer community for recent reports.
